name: Eterna
description: Costa blueberry cultivar launched in 2026 as one of the five BluGenix varieties. A single Eterna berry picked at Costa's Corindi farm on 13 November 2023 weighing 20.40 g and measuring 39.31 mm was recognised as the world's heaviest blueberry, beating a previous record of 16.20 g set in Western Australia in 2020. Company shelf-life claims of up to 50 days are separate marketing statements with no stated method.

attributes.identity_note: Commercial name only; no selection code, patent or plant breeders' right could be tied to it from the sources fetched.

record_berry.site: Costa berry farm, Corindi, New South Wales, Australia

traits.value: 20.40 g and 39.31 mm for the single record berry
traits.conditions: A single adjudicated fruit picked on 13 November 2023 at Corindi, New South Wales. A record specimen, not a representative fruit size for the cultivar. Reported by the owner and republished by trade media; the adjudicating body's own record page was not fetched.
traits.asserted_by: Guinness World Records, as reported by Costa Group

traits.conditions: Company claim at the BluGenix launch. No storage temperature, atmosphere, assessment criterion or trial is stated. A separate claim of 27 days at 4 degrees Celsius is made for all five BluGenix varieties including this one.
